title: Rabbi Acha bar (Rav) Ulla (Illa, Ila)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman maintains that all these names are of one single Amora, and adduces this proof: in Eruvin ch. 3, end of halakha 1, it states 'Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Ila said that all things are called food'; and this statement appears in Nedarim, beginning of ch. 6, as 'Rabbi Acha bar Ulla'; and in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 94, section 4, it is transmitted as 'Rabbi Acha bar Ilah'.
In Babylonia he was a student of Rav Chisda, as in Shabbat 54b: 'He was sitting before Rav Chisda and he sat and spoke --' Rav Chisda said to him, 'If so, you have made [the sheep into] Mar Ukva!'.

Afterwards he went to the Land of Israel, as we find him with Rabbi Zeira in Eruvin ch. 1, end of halakha 1, where he raised a difficulty against Rabbi Zeira, 'and why not'; and in Maaser Sheni ch. 5, halakha 3, 'Rabbi Yonah gave tithe to Rabbi Acha bar Ulla.'

He is mentioned in Tanchuma, Re'eh 12, where he asked, 'And is there Torah in the intestines?'; and in Eruvin 21b, Rav Papa son of Rav Aya bar Adda said in his name, 'From where [do we know] that whoever mocks the words of the Sages is judged in boiling excrement'; and in Shabbat 66a he is mentioned under the name Rav Acha bar Rav Ulla.

notes.text: The fuller Shabbat 54b account concerns a freshly shorn sheep treated with oil; Rav Chisda’s comparison is to Mar Ukva.

Shabbat 54b directly names Acha bar Ulla before Chisda and compares the oil-treated, freshly shorn sheep to Mar Ukva. Hyman’s emphatic single-Amora argument, migration and Ulla/Illa/Ila name equations remain his; no authority records are merged.
